title: Guest list
scenario: The RSVP list has duplicates. How many UNIQUE guests are coming?

intro.job: The RSVP list has duplicates. How many UNIQUE guests are coming?

idea.rule: len(guests) counts every copy — len(set(guests)) counts each one once.
idea.detail: set(some_list) builds a set: every value goes in, but a value that's already there is quietly dropped. So len(set(...)) counts how many DIFFERENT values there are. len(some_list) counts every entry, twins included.

model_restatement: Count how many different names are on the list, ignoring repeats.

clarify.question: Could the same name be spelled differently?
clarify.answer: No — today the names are clean and lowercase.

clarify.question: Do you want the names, or just how many?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Count the guests on the list and print the number.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 1, what is unique?

why_line: len(guests) counts every RSVP, so ana is counted three times — 5, not 3.

explain.rule: len(guests) is a headcount at the door that counts ana every time she walks in — three anas, three ticks.
explain.bridge: So what could you put the names into that keeps only one of each?

fix.rule: set(guests) throws out the twins first; len then counts what's left — one per person.

alternatives.note: The long way, with a list — slower on big lists, same answer.

hints: How many times does ana appear?
len counts every entry. You want each person once.

follow_up.prompt: New RSVPs: ['di', 'di', 'di'] — how many unique guests?
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — three dis are still one person.

one_liner: len(guests) counts every copy — len(set(guests)) counts each one once.
